system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING
PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the fatigue crack propagation law (Paris' Law: da/dN = C(ΔK)^m), where crack depth 'a' grows with each stress cycle. The key magnitude is the time from crack initiation to spall formation, which depends on stress amplitude, material toughness, and loading cycles. A 60-day prediction window requires detecting very early-stage crack growth before spall debris forms and causes temperature rise.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: Wayside acoustic station with microphone array (existing), wheel-impact-load-detector (existing), signal processing computer (new), acoustic signature database (new), crack growth model (new). Materials: Standard industrial-grade computing hardware. Procedure: Acoustic data from passing wheels is processed using time-frequency analysis (STFT) to identify bearing-specific signatures. Impact data provides loading history for crack growth modeling. A baseline healthy signature is established for each bearing type, and deviations are tracked against the crack growth model.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — The implementation burden is moderate (requires signal processing expertise and computing resources) compared to standard practice (manual visual inspection). Operability is improved (continuous monitoring vs. periodic), maintenance is similar (calibration of sensors), and cost class is comparable (capital expense vs. labor-intensive inspection). The approach is worth it for the safety benefit and elimination of depot visits.
EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install the system on a test track with instrumented bearings. Monitor bearings under controlled loading while introducing artificial surface defects of increasing severity. Instruments: Wayside acoustic station, thermocouples on axle boxes, accelerometers on bearings, strain gauges on axles. Pass/fail threshold: The system must detect acoustic signatures corresponding to crack depths that are at least 60 days away from spall formation (as confirmed by thermocouples showing temperature rise). Duration: Test until spall formation or 6 months, whichever comes first. Failure occurs if the system fails to predict the critical temperature rise with at least 60 days lead time in 95% of test cases.
